page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. A key hardware highlight is the inclusion of 15,359 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, which is Premium Storage capable, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, the L64as_v4 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core performance and a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core tests. Cryptographic and vector processing are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES. Memory performance is mixed, with small-block cached read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth scoring in the top 25%, while large-block uncached read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores remain in the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations both register strong performance, reflecting the high-throughput capabilities of the underlying NVMe storage and memory architecture.

The combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance highly cost-efficient for data-intensive workloads that require rapid local read/write access without the overhead of external storage arrays. It is well-suited for large relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, and high-throughput web serving. Additionally, its strong multi-threaded decompression and solid performance in small-to-medium LLM inference tasks support data engineering pipelines and localized machine learning inference workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure L64as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server from the Lasv4 family, powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 512.0 GB of RAM, and a massive 15,359 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong multi-core performance, scoring in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core benchmarks and the top 25% for database and Redis operations. The hardware includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES for accelerated cryptography and vector calculations. Lacking a GPU, it relies on its high-capacity local storage and balanced memory-to-CPU ratio to provide qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive applications. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and data engineering workloads.
